courses.title: Vase Family from One Master Profile
courses.objective: Draw one profile curve, build three different vases from it, then edit the profile once and watch every vase follow.

steps.title: Master profile
steps.learn: Every vase in this family reads the same curve. Change it later and all of them update.
instructions: Open a project and choose Model › Sketch on the XZ plane.
Draw a fit-point spline from the foot (small radius) up to the mouth.
X is the radius, Y is the height.
steps.why: One shared profile means one place to change the shape of the whole collection.

checkpoint.expected: An open spline, about 150 mm tall, wider in the middle.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase A: twisted flutes
steps.learn: A parametric vase turns the profile into a NURBS surface and then modulates it with flutes and a twist.
steps.why: Flutes, twist and sharpness are plain numbers you can edit at any time.

checkpoint.expected: A fluted surface with a gentle spiral.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase B: smooth and small
steps.learn: Setting flutes to 0 gives a smooth surface of revolution, here scaled to 80 %.
instructions: Create a second vase from the same profile.
Flutes 0, scale 0.8, height scale 0.8, position X 140.
steps.why: Scale and position let you build a set without drawing anything new.

checkpoint.expected: A second, smaller, smooth vase to the right.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase C: crystal
steps.learn: High sharpness makes the flutes crisp, and a negative twist spirals the other way.
instructions: Third vase: flutes 6, depth 0.14, sharpness 4, twist −90°.
steps.why: Sharpness 1 is soft and wavy, 4 is faceted like cut glass.

checkpoint.expected: A tall, crisp, spiralling vase on the left.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Edit the master profile once
steps.learn: Because all three vases reference one sketch, editing it updates the whole family at the same time.
instructions: Double-click “Vase profile” in the feature list.
Move the belly point out and the mouth point in.
Finish the sketch and watch all three vases change.
steps.why: This is what parametric means: the shape lives in one place, and everything derived from it is rebuilt.

checkpoint.expected: All three vases now have fuller bellies and narrower mouths.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Tune one vase only
steps.learn: Each vase also has its own numbers. Changing them affects that vase alone.
steps.why: Shared inputs (profile) and private inputs (flutes, twist) are what make a family.

checkpoint.expected: Vase A has a tighter spiral; B and C are unchanged.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a fourth member
steps.learn: A new vase costs one dialog, because the profile already exists.
instructions: Flutes 8, depth 0.1, sharpness 2.5, twist 0, scale 0.55, position Y −110.
steps.why: Designing a product range is mostly choosing different numbers for the same shapes.

checkpoint.expected: A small vase in front of the group.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken the hero vase
steps.learn: A surface has no thickness. Thicken offsets it into a closed solid you can export or print. Thicken cost grows quickly with the number of sections, so lower them first.
instructions: NURBS › Thicken: choose “Vase A · twisted flutes”, thickness 2.4 mm, density 3.
steps.why: A closed, valid solid is what STL, 3MF and STEP exports need. 36 × 12 sections keep 8 flutes clean and thicken in a few seconds.

checkpoint.expected: A solid wall of 2.4 mm on vase A.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Save and reuse
steps.learn: Save the project. Next time, change the profile and every vase follows.
instructions: Optional: Model › 3MF to export the thick vase for 3D printing.
steps.why: Keeping the design as history, not as a mesh, is what lets you come back and edit it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Twisted Fluted Vase to Printable Solid
courses.objective: Tune flutes, twist and sharpness on one vase, then thicken it into a printable solid and check it.

steps.title: Profile
steps.learn: A simple tall profile shows off the twist best.
instructions: Fit-point spline from foot to mouth.
steps.why: The profile decides the silhouette; the flutes only add relief.

checkpoint.expected: A slim, slightly bulging profile 160 mm tall.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Smooth vase first
steps.learn: Start with no flutes so you can see the plain shape.
steps.why: Build in stages: a smooth base first, then add relief.

checkpoint.expected: A smooth vase.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add flutes
steps.learn: Eight flutes at a shallow depth.
steps.why: Depth is a fraction of the local radius, so the flutes scale with the vase.

checkpoint.expected: Eight shallow flutes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a quarter twist
steps.learn: Twist turns the flutes as they climb.
steps.why: Twist is total rotation over the full height.

checkpoint.expected: The flutes spiral by a quarter turn.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Sharpen the edges
steps.learn: Sharpness 1 is soft, 4 is crisp.
steps.why: Crisp flutes catch light and read as cut glass.

checkpoint.expected: The flute ridges are now crisp.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Deeper flutes
steps.learn: Increase depth for a stronger relief.
steps.why: More relief means thicker material is needed later, so watch the wall thickness.

checkpoint.expected: Deeper valleys between the flutes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Reverse the spiral
steps.learn: A negative twist reverses the direction.
steps.why: Handedness is a design choice: pair a left and a right twist for a matching set.

checkpoint.expected: The spiral now runs the other way.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Choose the section count
steps.learn: More sections give a smoother surface, but Thicken time grows quickly with them. 36 around × 12 rows is a good balance for 8 flutes.
steps.why: Decide the resolution before the expensive step, not after it.

checkpoint.expected: The surface is slightly coarser but still crisp.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken to a solid
steps.learn: Offset the surface by the wall thickness to get a closed solid.
instructions: NURBS › Thicken: pick the vase, thickness 2.2 mm, density 3.
steps.why: A 2 mm wall prints well in most materials.

checkpoint.expected: A closed solid.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the mesh
steps.learn: Mesh check reports open or non-manifold edges and the volume.
steps.why: A printable model must be a closed shell with no open edges.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Export for printing
steps.learn: 3MF keeps millimetres and colours.
instructions: Open the file in your slicer.
steps.why: Always preview the first layers in the slicer before printing.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Egg-Core Vase Gallery
courses.objective: Shape three egg-form vases with bias, foot cut, mouth cut and scale, then thicken one.

steps.title: One egg
steps.learn: The egg core is a closed-form profile defined by five numbers; no sketch is needed.
steps.why: Bias moves the widest point up or down, which is what makes it egg-shaped.

checkpoint.expected: An egg-shaped open vase.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Slimmer, taller egg
steps.learn: Same tool, different numbers.
steps.why: You can read a lot about the shape just from the radius-to-height ratio.

checkpoint.expected: A tall, narrow egg.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wide bowl
steps.learn: A negative bias moves the belly low.
steps.why: Negative bias gives a bowl or a pear shape.

checkpoint.expected: A wide, low bowl.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Foot cut
steps.learn: Foot cut trims the bottom so the vase stands on a flat base.
steps.why: A flat foot is what stops a round vase from rolling.

checkpoint.expected: Egg 1 now stands on a wider foot.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mouth cut
steps.learn: Mouth cut sets the opening.
steps.why: A smaller opening suits stems; a wider one suits fruit.

checkpoint.expected: A narrower mouth on the tall egg.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Scale the group
steps.learn: Scale resizes a vase without touching its proportions.
steps.why: Scale keeps proportions; radius and height change them.

checkpoint.expected: The bowl is 15 % larger.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken one egg
steps.learn: Offset Egg 1 into a solid.
steps.why: Solids can be exported, sectioned and weighed.

checkpoint.expected: Egg 1 has a solid wall.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Compare
steps.learn: Look at the three shapes side by side.
instructions: Press F to fit the view.
steps.why: Comparing silhouettes side by side is how designers choose a form.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Pyramid & Dimpled Faceted Vases
courses.objective: Turn a profile into a faceted, hollow vase solid, then explore pyramid grids, dimples, density and wall thickness.

steps.title: Profile
steps.learn: The faceted vase also follows a profile sketch, so you can change the body shape at any time.
instructions: Draw an open spline from foot to mouth.
steps.why: The profile controls the outline; the facets only add the surface pattern.

checkpoint.expected: A barrel-shaped open profile.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Diamond facets
steps.learn: Faceted vase builds a closed, hollow solid directly: no Thicken step is needed.
instructions: Pattern Diamond, 14 around, 9 rows, depth 4 mm.
steps.why: Staggered diamonds read as a low-poly gem texture.

checkpoint.expected: A faceted solid vase.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pyramid grid
steps.learn: The pyramid pattern uses a square grid and looks like a pineapple.
steps.why: A square grid keeps rows aligned; a diamond grid offsets every second row.

checkpoint.expected: Square pyramids in aligned rows.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Dimples instead of bumps
steps.learn: A negative depth pushes the facets inward.
steps.why: Sign changes the look completely: bumps catch light, dimples hold shadow.

checkpoint.expected: Pyramid dimples.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Finer texture
steps.learn: More facets with a shallower depth give a fine texture.
instructions: Pattern Diamond, 28 around, 18 rows, depth 2 mm.
steps.why: Texture scale should match the size of the object and the process that makes it.

checkpoint.expected: A fine diamond texture.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Edit the profile
steps.learn: Changing the profile reshapes the vase and rebuilds every facet.
instructions: Move the belly point out and the mouth point in.
steps.why: The facets follow the surface, because they are generated from the profile every time.

checkpoint.expected: A rounder, fuller vase with the same facet pattern.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wall and base
steps.learn: Wall is the shell thickness, base is the floor thickness.
steps.why: Thin walls save material; a thicker base keeps the vase stable.

checkpoint.expected: A thinner wall and a heavier floor.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: A companion piece
steps.learn: Reuse the same profile for a second vase with a different pattern, placed beside the first.
instructions: Pyramid grid, 14 around, 9 rows, depth 5, position X 170.
steps.why: Two surfaces from one profile make a matching pair.

checkpoint.expected: Two matching vases with different textures.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check and export
steps.learn: Both vases are closed solids, so they can be printed directly.
instructions: Select a vase, Model › Mesh check.
steps.why: Run the check before every export. A hole in the mesh is far cheaper to find now than after a print.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Wavy-Rib Lattice Vase
courses.objective: Build a woven lattice of tubes around an egg core and tune ribs, waves, amplitude and tube radius.

steps.title: Egg core
steps.learn: The core gives the lattice its shape. The lattice uses the same five shape numbers.
steps.why: The lattice reads the same radius, height and bias, so it hugs whatever core you choose.

checkpoint.expected: An egg-shaped open vase.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: One family of wavy ribs
steps.learn: Each rib is a tube that follows the egg surface and swings left and right as it climbs.
instructions: Ribs 12, waves 3, amplitude 0.32, tube 2.6, one family.
steps.why: A single family of ribs is a wavy cage; two families weave.

checkpoint.expected: Twelve wavy tubes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weave a second family
steps.learn: The second family swings the opposite way, so the ribs cross.
steps.why: Two families give the diamond mesh of a basket.

checkpoint.expected: A woven lattice.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: More waves
steps.learn: Waves counts how many times a rib swings across the height.
steps.why: More waves make a busier, tighter weave.

checkpoint.expected: The crossings are more frequent.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Stronger swing
steps.learn: Amplitude is the sideways swing in radians.
steps.why: Large amplitude opens big diamonds, small amplitude gives near-vertical ribs.

checkpoint.expected: Larger diamonds.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Finer ribs
steps.learn: Thinner tubes and more of them.
steps.why: Rib count and tube radius together set how open the lattice looks.

checkpoint.expected: A finer, lighter lattice.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Gap to the core
steps.learn: Lift floats the lattice away from the core surface.
steps.why: A gap lets you see the core through the lattice, or remove the core completely later.

checkpoint.expected: The ribs float off the core.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rims
steps.learn: Rims are the circular tubes that close the top and the foot.
instructions: Turn rims off, then on again.
steps.why: Rims tie the ribs together so the lattice reads as one object.

checkpoint.expected: Rim rings at the top and the foot.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: A second vase
steps.learn: Reuse the idea at a different size, with a stronger swing.
instructions: Add another egg core and lattice: radius 44, height 150, position X 170.
steps.why: Changing two numbers per vase builds a coherent product family.

checkpoint.expected: A smaller second vase beside the first.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
